scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original A2 pilot bank for A Small Change, a Better Result; independent questions on the original passage; not pedagogically approved.

tabs.title: Understanding the story
tabs.description: Choose what the story tells us.

questions.q: What is Daniel trying to change before Thursday's test?
choices: The time his science lesson starts.
The subject of the test.
The way he prepares during the week.
The teacher who marks his answers.
questions.explanation: Daniel replaces last-minute study with a plan that spreads practice through the week.

questions.q: How was Daniel's old plan different from his new plan?
choices: He used to study late on one evening.
He used to study with his sister every day.
He used to work for only twenty minutes.
He used to take many breaks on Wednesday.
questions.explanation: Daniel usually studied everything on Wednesday night and felt tired the next day.

questions.q: What does Daniel discover when he explains an idea to his sister?
choices: His teacher has given the wrong homework.
He needs to write his notes again.
She already knows everything.
He does not understand every part clearly.
questions.explanation: Explaining the idea helps Daniel notice what he still needs to check.

questions.q: Which part of Daniel's result pleases him most?
choices: His result was the highest in his class.
He prepared calmly and slept well.
He answered every question correctly.
His sister helped during the test.
questions.explanation: Daniel is especially pleased with sleeping well and enjoying his Wednesday evening.

questions.q: Why does Daniel answer questions without looking at the answers?
choices: To show his sister that the book is easy.
To make the questions shorter.
To find out what he can remember.
To practise writing very quickly.
questions.explanation: Trying questions without answers lets Daniel check what he can do by himself.

questions.q: Why does Daniel turn off phone notifications?
choices: He is waiting for an important message.
He wants to save the phone battery.
He has lost his phone at school.
He wants fewer interruptions while studying.
questions.explanation: Switching off notifications is part of Daniel's more focused study plan.

questions.q: Why does Daniel write down things to practise after the test?
choices: He wants to work on the things he missed.
He wants to copy his friend's answers.
He thinks the teacher will cancel the test.
He wants to forget the difficult questions.
questions.explanation: After making two mistakes, Daniel records what he still needs to practise.

questions.q: A friend cannot explain a science idea. What could Daniel suggest?
choices: Read the answer without thinking about it.
Move on and forget that part.
Check the notes and look for an example.
Study for three hours without stopping.
questions.explanation: Daniel checks his notes and uses a textbook example when he does not understand.

questions.q: A student gets a good mark but feels very tired. What can they learn from Daniel?
choices: They should not prepare for the next test.
Rest and a calmer plan are important too.
Only the mark matters after a test.
They should study longer next time.
questions.explanation: Daniel values getting enough sleep as well as improving his mark.

questions.q: Daniel wants to study history next week. Which plan fits the story?
choices: Try the useful parts of his plan and make changes if needed.
Use the same questions as in science.
Wait until the night before his history test.
Ask his sister to learn the facts for him.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph says Daniel plans to use the approach for history and adjust it if necessary.
